audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Deuteronomy / Devarim not-by-righteousness, golden-calf, and Moses-intercession discourse, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for conquest warning against self-righteousness, Anakim, dispossession rhetoric, Horeb fast, calf apostasy, broken tablets, Aaron intercession, Taberah/Massah/Kibroth memory, Kadesh refusal, and forty-day intercession.

verses.restored: Hear, Israel: You are crossing Jordan today to enter and possess nations greater and mightier than you, cities great and fortified to heavens,

familiar.text: Hear, O Israel: Thou art to pass over Jordan this day, to go in to possess nations greater and mightier than thyself, cities great and fenced up to heaven,

modern.text: Hear, O Israel: Today you are about to cross the Jordan to go in and dispossess nations greater and stronger than you, with large cities fortified to the heavens.

original.text: שְׁמַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אַתָּ֨ה עֹבֵ֤ר הַיּוֹם֙ אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לָבֹא֙ לָרֶ֣שֶׁת גּוֹיִ֔ם גְּדֹלִ֥ים וַעֲצֻמִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑ךָּ עָרִ֛ים גְּדֹלֹ֥ת וּבְצֻרֹ֖ת בַּשָּׁמָֽיִם

verses.restored: a people great and tall, sons of Anakim, whom you know and of whom you heard, Who can stand before sons of Anak?

familiar.text: A people great and tall, the children of the Anakims, whom thou knowest, and of whom thou hast heard say, Who can stand before the children of Anak!

modern.text: The people are strong and tall, the descendants of the Anakim. You know about them, and you have heard it said, “Who can stand up to the sons of Anak?”

original.text: עַֽם גָּד֥וֹל וָרָ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י עֲנָקִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֨עְתָּ֙ וְאַתָּ֣ה שָׁמַ֔עְתָּ מִ֣י יִתְיַצֵּ֔ב לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י עֲנָֽק

verses.restored: Know today that YHWH your Divine is crossing before you as consuming fire; he will destroy them and humble them before you, and you shall dispossess and cause them to perish quickly, as YHWH spoke to you.

familiar.text: Understand therefore this day, that the LORD thy God is he which goeth over before thee; as a consuming fire he shall destroy them, and he shall bring them down before thy face: so shalt thou drive them out, and destroy them quickly, as the LORD hath said unto thee.

modern.text: But understand that today the LORD your God goes across ahead of you as a consuming fire; He will destroy them and subdue them before you. And you will drive them out and annihilate them swiftly, as the LORD has promised you.

original.text: וְיָדַעְתָּ֣ הַיּ֗וֹם כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ הֽוּא הָעֹבֵ֤ר לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ אֵ֣שׁ אֹֽכְלָ֔ה ה֧וּא יַשְׁמִידֵ֛ם וְה֥וּא יַכְנִיעֵ֖ם לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וְהֽוֹרַשְׁתָּ֤ם וְהַֽאַבַדְתָּם֙ מַהֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָֽךְ

verses.restored: Do not say in your heart, when YHWH your Divine thrusts them out from before you, Because of my righteousness YHWH brought me in to possess this land; rather, because of wickedness of these nations YHWH dispossesses them from before you.

familiar.text: Speak not thou in thine heart, after that the LORD thy God hath cast them out from before thee, saying, For my righteousness the LORD hath brought me in to possess this land: but for the wickedness of these nations the LORD doth drive them out from before thee.

modern.text: When the LORD your God has driven them out before you, do not say in your heart, “Because of my righteousness the LORD has brought me in to possess this land.” Rather, the LORD is driving out these nations before you because of their wickedness.

original.text: אַל תֹּאמַ֣ר בִּלְבָבְךָ֗ בַּהֲדֹ֣ף יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ אֹתָ֥ם מִלְּפָנֶיךָ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ בְּצִדְקָתִי֙ הֱבִיאַ֣נִי יְהוָ֔ה לָרֶ֖שֶׁת אֶת הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את וּבְרִשְׁעַת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֔לֶּה יְהוָ֖ה מוֹרִישָׁ֥ם מִפָּנֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Not because of your righteousness or uprightness of your heart are you entering to possess their land, but because of wickedness of these nations YHWH your Divine dispossesses them and to establish word YHWH swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

familiar.text: Not for thy righteousness, or for the uprightness of thine heart, dost thou go to possess their land: but for the wickedness of these nations the LORD thy God doth drive them out from before thee, and that he may perform the word which the LORD sware unto thy fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

modern.text: It is not because of your righteousness or uprightness of heart that you are going in to possess their land, but it is because of their wickedness that the LORD your God is driving out these nations before you, to keep the promise He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

original.text: לֹ֣א בְצִדְקָתְךָ֗ וּבְיֹ֨שֶׁר֙ לְבָ֣בְךָ֔ אַתָּ֥ה בָ֖א לָרֶ֣שֶׁת אֶת אַרְצָ֑ם כִּ֞י בְּרִשְׁעַ֣ת הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֗לֶּה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ מוֹרִישָׁ֣ם מִפָּנֶ֔יךָ וּלְמַ֜עַן הָקִ֣ים אֶת הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע יְהוָה֙ לַאֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹֽב

verses.restored: Know that not because of your righteousness YHWH your Divine gives you this good land to possess, for a stiff-necked people are you.

familiar.text: Understand therefore, that the LORD thy God giveth thee not this good land to possess it for thy righteousness; for thou art a stiffnecked people.

modern.text: Understand, then, that it is not because of your righteousness that the LORD your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stiff-necked people. The Golden Calf (Exodus 32:1–35; Acts 7:39–43)

original.text: וְיָדַעְתָּ֗ כִּ֠י לֹ֤א בְצִדְקָֽתְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱ֠לֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵ֨ן לְךָ֜ אֶת הָאָ֧רֶץ הַטּוֹבָ֛ה הַזֹּ֖את לְרִשְׁתָּ֑הּ כִּ֥י עַם קְשֵׁה עֹ֖רֶף אָֽתָּה

verses.restored: Remember, do not forget, how you provoked YHWH your Divine in wilderness; from day you came out from land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebellious with YHWH.

familiar.text: Remember, and forget not, how thou provokedst the LORD thy God to wrath in the wilderness: from the day that thou didst depart out of the land of Egypt, until ye came unto this place, ye have been rebellious against the LORD.

modern.text: Remember this, and never forget how you provoked the LORD your God in the wilderness. From the day you left the land of Egypt until you reached this place, you have been rebelling against the LORD.

original.text: זְכֹר֙ אַל תִּשְׁכַּ֔ח אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר הִקְצַ֛פְתָּ אֶת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר לְמִן הַיּ֞וֹם אֲשֶׁר יָצָ֣אתָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם עַד בֹּֽאֲכֶם֙ עַד הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה מַמְרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם עִם יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: At Horeb you provoked YHWH, and YHWH was angry with you to destroy you.

familiar.text: Also in Horeb ye provoked the LORD to wrath, so that the LORD was angry with you to have destroyed you.

modern.text: At Horeb you provoked the LORD, and He was angry enough to destroy you.

original.text: וּבְחֹרֵ֥ב הִקְצַפְתֶּ֖ם אֶת יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתְאַנַּ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה בָּכֶ֖ם לְהַשְׁמִ֥יד אֶתְכֶֽם

verses.restored: When I went up mountain to receive tablets of stone, tablets of covenant YHWH cut with you, I remained on mountain forty days and forty nights; bread I did not eat and water I did not drink.

familiar.text: When I was gone up into the mount to receive the tables of stone, even the tables of the covenant which the LORD made with you, then I abode in the mount forty days and forty nights, I neither did eat bread nor drink water:

modern.text: When I went up on the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that the LORD made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.

original.text: בַּעֲלֹתִ֣י הָהָ֗רָה לָקַ֜חַת לוּחֹ֤ת הָֽאֲבָנִים֙ לוּחֹ֣ת הַבְּרִ֔ית אֲשֶׁר כָּרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּכֶ֑ם וָאֵשֵׁ֣ב בָּהָ֗ר אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יוֹם֙ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים לַ֔יְלָה לֶ֚חֶם לֹ֣א אָכַ֔לְתִּי וּמַ֖יִם לֹ֥א שָׁתִֽיתִי

verses.restored: YHWH gave me two tablets of stone written with finger of Divine, and upon them according to all words YHWH spoke with you at mountain from midst of fire on day of assembly.

familiar.text: And the LORD delivered unto me two tables of stone written with the finger of God; and on them was written according to all the words, which the LORD spake with you in the mount out of the midst of the fire in the day of the assembly.

modern.text: Then the LORD gave me the two stone tablets, inscribed by the finger of God with the exact words that the LORD spoke to you out of the fire on the mountain on the day of the assembly.

original.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י אֶת שְׁנֵי֙ לוּחֹ֣ת הָֽאֲבָנִ֔ים כְּתֻבִ֖ים בְּאֶצְבַּ֣ע אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַעֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כְּֽכָל הַדְּבָרִ֡ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּר֩ יְהוָ֨ה עִמָּכֶ֥ם בָּהָ֛ר מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֵ֖שׁ בְּי֥וֹם הַקָּהָֽל

verses.restored: At end of forty days and forty nights YHWH gave me two tablets of stone, tablets of covenant.

familiar.text: And it came to pass at the end of forty days and forty nights, that the LORD gave me the two tables of stone, even the tables of the covenant.

modern.text: And at the end of forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י מִקֵּץ֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָ֑יְלָה נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י אֶת שְׁנֵ֛י לֻחֹ֥ת הָאֲבָנִ֖ים לֻח֥וֹת הַבְּרִֽית

verses.restored: YHWH said to me, Rise, go down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out from Egypt have acted corruptly; they turned quickly from way I commanded them and made for themselves molten image.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto me, Arise, get thee down quickly from hence; for thy people which thou hast brought forth out of Egypt have corrupted themselves; they are quickly turned aside out of the way which I commanded them; they have made them a molten image.

modern.text: And the LORD said to me, “Get up and go down from here at once, for your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. How quickly they have turned aside from the way that I commanded them! They have made for themselves a molten image.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י ק֣וּם רֵ֤ד מַהֵר֙ מִזֶּ֔ה כִּ֚י שִׁחֵ֣ת עַמְּךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹצֵ֖אתָ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם סָ֣רוּ מַהֵ֗ר מִן הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ם עָשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם מַסֵּכָֽה

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to me, saying, I have seen this people, and look, a stiff-necked people it is.

familiar.text: Furthermore the LORD spake unto me, saying, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people:

modern.text: The LORD also said to me, “I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stiff-necked people.

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֑ר רָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה עַם קְשֵׁה עֹ֖רֶף הֽוּא

verses.restored: Let me alone, and I will destroy them and blot out their name from under heavens, and I will make you a nation mightier and more numerous than they.

familiar.text: Let me alone, that I may destroy them, and blot out their name from under heaven: and I will make of thee a nation mightier and greater than they.

modern.text: Leave Me alone, so that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven. Then I will make you into a nation mightier and greater than they are.”

original.text: הֶ֤רֶף מִמֶּ֨נִּי֙ וְאַשְׁמִידֵ֔ם וְאֶמְחֶ֣ה אֶת שְׁמָ֔ם מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ אֽוֹתְךָ֔ לְגוֹי עָצ֥וּם וָרָ֖ב מִמֶּֽנּוּ

verses.restored: I turned and went down from mountain while mountain burned with fire, and two tablets of covenant were in my two hands.

familiar.text: So I turned and came down from the mount, and the mount burned with fire: and the two tables of the covenant were in my two hands.

modern.text: So I went back down the mountain while it was blazing with fire, with the two tablets of the covenant in my hands.

original.text: וָאֵ֗פֶן וָֽאֵרֵד֙ מִן הָהָ֔ר וְהָהָ֖ר בֹּעֵ֣ר בָּאֵ֑שׁ וּשְׁנֵי֙ לֻחֹ֣ת הַבְּרִ֔ית עַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֥י יָדָֽי

verses.restored: I saw, and look, you had sinned/misaligned against YHWH your Divine; you made for yourselves a molten calf. You turned quickly from way YHWH commanded you.

familiar.text: And I looked, and, behold, ye had sinned against the LORD your God, and had made you a molten calf: ye had turned aside quickly out of the way which the LORD had commanded you.

modern.text: And I saw how you had sinned against the LORD your God; you had made for yourselves a molten calf. You had turned aside quickly from the way that the LORD had commanded you.

original.text: וָאֵ֗רֶא וְהִנֵּ֤ה חֲטָאתֶם֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם עֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם לָכֶ֔ם עֵ֖גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה סַרְתֶּ֣ם מַהֵ֔ר מִן הַדֶּ֕רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶתְכֶֽם

verses.restored: I seized two tablets and threw them from my two hands and broke them before your eyes.

familiar.text: And I took the two tables, and cast them out of my two hands, and brake them before your eyes.

modern.text: So I took the two tablets and threw them out of my hands, shattering them before your eyes.

original.text: וָאֶתְפֹּשׂ֙ בִּשְׁנֵ֣י הַלֻּחֹ֔ת וָֽאַשְׁלִכֵ֔ם מֵעַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֣י יָדָ֑י וָאֲשַׁבְּרֵ֖ם לְעֵינֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: I fell before YHWH as at first, forty days and forty nights; bread I did not eat and water I did not drink, because of all your sin/misalignment you sinned, doing evil in eyes of YHWH to provoke him.

familiar.text: And I fell down before the LORD, as at the first, forty days and forty nights: I did neither eat bread, nor drink water, because of all your sins which ye sinned, in doing wickedly in the sight of the LORD, to provoke him to anger.

modern.text: Then I fell down before the LORD for forty days and forty nights, as I had done the first time. I did not eat bread or drink water because of all the sin you had committed in doing what was evil in the sight of the LORD and provoking Him to anger.

original.text: וָֽאֶתְנַפַּל֩ לִפְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה כָּרִאשֹׁנָ֗ה אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יוֹם֙ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים לַ֔יְלָה לֶ֚חֶם לֹ֣א אָכַ֔לְתִּי וּמַ֖יִם לֹ֣א שָׁתִ֑יתִי עַ֤ל כָּל חַטַּאתְכֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֲטָאתֶ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִיסֽוֹ

verses.restored: For I feared anger and fury with which YHWH was angry against you to destroy you. But YHWH listened to me also that time.

familiar.text: For I was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure, wherewith the LORD was wroth against you to destroy you. But the LORD hearkened unto me at that time also.

modern.text: For I was afraid of the anger and wrath that the LORD had directed against you, enough to destroy you. But the LORD listened to me this time as well.

original.text: כִּ֣י יָגֹ֗רְתִּי מִפְּנֵ֤י הָאַף֙ וְהַ֣חֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר קָצַ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם לְהַשְׁמִ֣יד אֶתְכֶ֑ם וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י גַּ֖ם בַּפַּ֥עַם הַהִֽוא

verses.restored: Against Aaron YHWH was very angry to destroy him, and I prayed also for Aaron at that time.

familiar.text: And the LORD was very angry with Aaron to have destroyed him: and I prayed for Aaron also the same time.

modern.text: The LORD was angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, but at that time I also prayed for Aaron.

original.text: וּֽבְאַהֲרֹ֗ן הִתְאַנַּ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה מְאֹ֖ד לְהַשְׁמִיד֑וֹ וָֽאֶתְפַּלֵּ֛ל גַּם בְּעַ֥ד אַהֲרֹ֖ן בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽוא

verses.restored: Your sin/misalignment that you made, calf, I took and burned with fire, crushed it, grinding thoroughly until fine as dust, and threw its dust into brook descending from mountain.

familiar.text: And I took your sin, the calf which ye had made, and burnt it with fire, and stamped it, and ground it very small, even until it was as small as dust: and I cast the dust thereof into the brook that descended out of the mount.

modern.text: And I took that sinful thing, the calf you had made, and burned it in the fire. Then I crushed it and ground it to powder as fine as dust, and I cast it into the stream that came down from the mountain.

original.text: וְֽאֶת חַטַּאתְכֶ֞ם אֲשֶׁר עֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם אֶת הָעֵ֗גֶל לָקַחְתִּי֮ וָאֶשְׂרֹ֣ף אֹת֣וֹ בָּאֵשׁ֒ וָאֶכֹּ֨ת אֹת֤וֹ טָחוֹן֙ הֵיטֵ֔ב עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר דַּ֖ק לְעָפָ֑ר וָֽאַשְׁלִךְ֙ אֶת עֲפָר֔וֹ אֶל הַנַּ֖חַל הַיֹּרֵ֥ד מִן הָהָֽר

verses.restored: At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah you provoked YHWH.

familiar.text: And at Taberah, and at Massah, and at Kibrothhattaavah, ye provoked the LORD to wrath.

modern.text: You continued to provoke the LORD at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah.

translation_notes: The chapter's central claim is anti-triumphal: possession is not proof of Israel's superior righteousness.
Calling conquered nations wicked does not morally solve the violence of dispossession or permit later empires to label targeted peoples evil.
Stiff-necked language is internal covenant critique, not permission for antisemitic stereotypes about Jewish stubbornness or rejection.
Moses refuses the offer to replace Israel with a nation descended from himself and intercedes for the threatened people.
His fasting is narrative intercession, not a mandate for medically dangerous fasting or self-punishment.
The broken tablets embody covenant rupture, while Moses' repeated prayer preserves the possibility of renewal.
safety_note: Do not use Deuteronomy 9 to justify conquest by declaring another people wicked, to promote antisemitic 'stiff-necked' tropes, or to claim success proves righteousness. Center humility, refusal of replacement theology, leadership that intercedes rather than profits from destruction, and covenant renewal after failure.
